summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration file that defines a single service called 'app'. It specifies how to build a Docker image from a Dockerfile, sets up environment variables for the application, exposes port 8000, and configures security and networking settings for the container.

explanations.4: The 'build' section tells Docker Compose how to construct the image instead of pulling it from a registry.
explanations.5: The 'context' is the directory Docker will use as the root when building—it'll look for the Dockerfile and any files to copy relative to this path.
explanations.7: The 'args' are build-time variables passed to the Dockerfile's RUN commands; they're only available during the image construction phase.
explanations.12: The 'environment' section sets runtime variables that will be available inside the running container; these are different from build args.
explanations.16: This specifies what the built image should be named and tagged as; Docker will reference this name when creating containers.
explanations.18: Setting 'default' to null means the service uses the default network but doesn't add any custom configuration to it.
explanations.20: The 'mode: ingress' means the port is published at the gateway level, making it accessible from outside the Docker host.
explanations.26: The 'user' specifies which user ID and group ID the container's processes will run as; '1001:1001' is a non-root user for security.
